# Fixed K33 cannot have a uniform small all-input readout TV error

Status: DIRECTED SYMBOLIC CROSS-CHECK / SHARED AUTHOR CONTEXT / UNREVIEWED / NOT ADMITTED.

The contraction route was proposed by the sparse agent; the default-width input family and explicit algebraic-norm bound were proposed by the root. This note audits the logic, supplies the ideal tail and realification details, and uses the simplified family that is never a perfect power. It is not independent admission.

Researcher: `EM-DIRECT-C6438C`; activity: `RA-CAAAC604CB513AEA8BBC1DFC`.
Registration Source: `f0e5fb6f478a5a380ab5a7533d2585f7f43ee3bf`.
Pinned K33 bank payload SHA256: `feecbc02808991f6d7b1e2c3179c8da2018b76901ef34c26ef0d28b65729dd5c`.

No actual or ideal new trajectory, Fourier reference, trigonometric evaluation, order-search execution, or higher-precision run is used. All limits below are symbolic. No file in the stabilized `next_cf_only/` unit is changed.

## 1. Conclusion and the distribution to which it applies

Fix an order `r=2^s d`, with `d>3` odd. Compare the complete raw control-readout distributions of:

- the actual full-mode fixed K33 streaming algorithm, and
- the ideal Shor order-finding circuit with the same `N,a,t` and initial state.

As allowed even widths `t` tend to infinity while the order stays fixed,

`liminf TV(P_K33,t, P_ideal,t) >= 1-gcd(d,3)/d`.

Moreover, for every fixed odd prime `p>=5`, there is an explicit infinite family of odd non-prime-power composite inputs and good bases having order `2p`, with the standard width `t=2 ceil(log2 N)`, for which

`lim TV = 1-1/p`.

Since such primes are arbitrarily large, **no constant epsilon<1 can bound this raw readout TV for every allowed `(N,a,t)` under the fixed K33 bank**, even when `t` is always the default width and the base is good. The supremum of these conditional readout TV errors over the permitted inputs is one; this is a supremum statement, not a claim that a finite example attains TV exactly one.

The theorem is about readouts conditional on the specified base. It does not automatically give the same lower bound after averaging over a random-base strategy, or after CF/gcd postprocessing into factor/failed statuses. Those operations can reduce TV. It also does not contradict the positive CF-success support and finite-retry theorem: success support and uniform closeness to the ideal full distribution are different claims.

## 2. The finite product/phase family gives a strictly positive contraction constant

Use the exact actual streaming recurrence. On a complexified work eigencomponent of eigenvalue `lambda`, round `i` has two internal branch maps

`K_(sigma,mu,T)=(I+sigma mu T)/2`, with `sigma in {+1,-1}`,

`mu=lambda^(2^(t-1-i))`.

The full actual history product `T` is a fixed-order subset product of `V_2,...,V_32`; all higher phase indices are full-dimensional identities. Therefore there are at most `2^31` such products, independently of `N,t`.

Every `T` is rational and real orthogonal. By the already proved near-rank-two cyclotomic exclusion, no such `T` has a root-of-unity eigenvalue of degree at least four. The proof uses the actual uniform distance `177*2^-32<1/2` from a principal-plane rotation plus the identity: all but two eigenvalue distances from one are small, and any cyclotomic factor of degree `f>=4` would force the nonzero integer `|Phi_L(1)|` below one. See `next_cf_only/ROOT_CF_ALL_WIDTH_SUCCESS.md`, Section 3.

Call a work eigencomponent high-odd-part if its eigenvalue order has odd part greater than three. Raising it to a power of two preserves that odd part. Thus every possible `-sigma mu^(-1)` in this class has cyclotomic degree at least four, and neither branch matrix can be singular.

For fixed `r`, the possible work eigenvalues belong to the finite set of `r`th roots; so do all `mu`. Let `U_high(r)` be the finite superset of those roots whose order has odd part greater than three. Define the number

`c_*(r) = min_(mu in U_high(r), T in finite_masks, sigma=+/-1)`

`          smallest_singular_value((I+sigma mu T)/2)^2`.

Each entry in this finite minimum is strictly positive, hence `c_*(r)>0`. The minimum is taken on the full internal carrier. It depends on the fixed order and fixed bank, but not on the width, input size, work labels, or history. The next calculation supplies an explicit lower bound without enumerating these matrices.

### 2.1 An explicit algebraic-norm lower bound

There are at most 30 retained nonexact phase factors, each with entry denominator dividing `2^128`; the quarter-turn is integral. Thus every product `T` has entry denominator dividing `2^K`, with `K=3840`. Let `D=61`, let `F=I+sigma mu T`, and put `A=2^K F`. The entries of `A` lie in `Z[mu]`, so `det A` is an algebraic integer. It is nonzero by the cyclotomic exclusion already proved.

Write `f=[Q(mu):Q]`. Here `f=phi(ord(mu))<=r`. Every field embedding sends `mu` to another unit-modulus root of unity and fixes `T`. Hence each conjugate matrix `A^(tau)` has norm at most `2^(K+1)` and determinant modulus at most `2^(D(K+1))`. The nonzero field norm of `det A` is an integer of absolute value at least one. Bounding all other `f-1` factors yields

`|det A| >= 2^(-D(K+1)(f-1))`,

`|det F| >= 2^(-D[(K+1)f-1])`.

All singular values of `F` are at most two. Dividing its determinant by the product of the other `D-1` singular values gives

`smallest_singular_value(F/2) >= 2^(-D(K+1)f)`.

Consequently the uniform explicit squared lower bound

`c_r := 2^(-2D(K+1)r) = 2^(-468602 r)`

satisfies `0<c_r<=c_*(r)`. This is a symbolic algebraic-integer estimate from actual word denominators, not a numerical singular-value computation. The value is deliberately very conservative.

For each fixed `mu,T`, because `mu T` is unitary on the complexified internal space,

`K_+^* K_+ + K_-^* K_- = I`.

Both branches have smallest singular value squared at least `c_r`. Using the **other branch's** lower bound gives

`K_sigma^* K_sigma <= (1-c_r) I`.

Thus `0<c_r<=1/2` and each branch contracts squared norm by at most the factor `1-c_r`. This step does not follow from invertibility alone without the finiteness and completeness arguments.

Along any particular length-`t` history, a high-odd-part work component therefore has final squared norm at most `(1-c_r)^t` times its initial squared norm. The bound is uniform over all bins, even though the actual selected products vary with the history.

## 3. Initial spectral weights and the exceptional mass

The work orbit from `|1>` has length `r`; its `r` Fourier eigenvectors are orthonormal, and each has initial squared weight `1/r`. All work operations are powers of the same orbit permutation; each history-dependent phase acts only on the internal factor. Hence the algorithm never mixes these work eigenspaces, including after branching. Orthogonality prevents cancellation between different work components, and branch completeness preserves each component's total mass when all readouts are summed.

Index the eigenvalues by `lambda_j=exp(2 pi i j/r)`, `0<=j<r`. Their order's odd part is

`d/gcd(d,j)`.

This equals one or three exactly when `d` divides `3j`. Among the `d` residue classes of `j`, there are `gcd(d,3)` solutions; each repeats `2^s` times among the `r` eigenvalues. The total exceptional initial weight is therefore exactly

`w_low = gcd(d,3)/d`, and `w_high=1-w_low`.

For any set `A` of readout bins, the exceptional components can contribute at most `w_low` in total. The uniform per-bin bound for the other components gives

`P_K33,t(A) <= w_low + |A| w_high (1-c_r)^t`.

No assumption is made about the detailed dynamics or support of the exceptional components. The counting remains valid when `d` is divisible by higher powers of three; for example, `d=9` gives `w_low=1/3`, not one.

## 4. Ideal phase-estimation peaks have a symbolic inverse-radius tail

For the standard ideal eigenphase `j/r`, the finite-`Q` phase-estimation kernel is

`F_(Q,j)(k) = |(1/Q) sum_(x=0)^(Q-1) exp(2 pi i x(j/r-k/Q))|^2`.

This formula is used only symbolically. Let `D_Q(k,Qj/r)` be the circular distance between `k` and `Qj/r` on the circle of circumference `Q`, taking values in `[0,Q/2]`. If that distance is nonzero, the exact finite geometric-sum identity and the numerator bound give

`F_(Q,j)(k) <= 1/[Q^2 sin^2(pi D_Q/Q)]`.

For `0<=x<=pi/2`, the chord inequality gives `sin x>=2x/pi`. Therefore

`F_(Q,j)(k) <= 1/[4 D_Q(k,Qj/r)^2]`.

For each integer shell `h<=D_Q<h+1`, there are at most two integer bins. For integer radius `L>=2`, the mass outside the circular radius-`L` neighborhood of the center is consequently at most

`(1/2) sum_(h=L)^infinity 1/h^2 <= 1/[2(L-1)]`.

If the center is itself an integer, its exact point mass causes no difficulty; the tail outside the neighborhood is zero in that component.

Let `A_(t,L)` be the union of these neighborhoods around all `r` centers `Qj/r`. It contains at most `r(2L+1)` bins. The ideal mixture therefore obeys

`P_ideal,t(A_(t,L)) >= 1-1/[2(L-1)]`.

No separation or disjointness of the windows is needed for either bound. For the limit one may simply take `L=t`, with sufficiently large allowed even `t`; then the window has only `O(r t)` bins while its ideal probability tends to one.

## 5. Realification and the two internal phase planes do not alter this ideal law

The ideal replacement acts only on the first two real coordinates and fixes all residual coordinates. Starting at `e0`, that two-dimensional real plane is the usual representation of a complex scalar; real work permutations and the real Hadamard preparation commute with this representation. Summing squares of the two real coordinates is exactly the complex modulus square. Under this direct realification identification, the ideal full circuit gives the standard Shor control-readout distribution.

There is a subtlety if one instead uses the proof's complexification of the real work/internal space. A fixed complexified work eigenblock alone does not generally have just one phase-estimation kernel. The real planar rotation has two complex eigenlines, with conjugate phase factors, and

`e0=(u_+ + u_-)/sqrt(2)`

for normalized orthogonal eigenvectors. Thus a work eigenblock of index `j` contributes a half-weight kernel for one phase orientation and a half-weight kernel for the conjugate orientation. Its conditional ideal readout is

`(F_(Q,j)(k)+F_(Q,-j)(k))/2`,

up to the immaterial choice of which eigenline is named plus. Each work block has weight `1/r`. On summing all `j`, the substitution `j -> -j mod r` gives exactly

`P_ideal,t(k)=(1/r) sum_(j=0)^(r-1) F_(Q,j)(k)`.

There is no extra factor of two and no additional residual-mode probability in the ideal initial condition. The union of all `r` peak neighborhoods is also invariant under sign reversal, so the concentration bound of Section 4 would remain valid directly under the two-kernel description.

The actual algorithm can populate residual modes, and Section 2 deliberately bounds it on the entire carrier. It does not assume actual dynamics remain in the principal plane.

## 6. Total-variation lower bound at fixed order

Take `A_t=A_(t,t)`. The preceding sections give

`P_ideal,t(A_t) >= 1-1/[2(t-1)]`,

`P_K33,t(A_t) <= w_low + r(2t+1) w_high (1-c_r)^t`.

Since total variation is at least the difference of probabilities of any event,

`TV(P_K33,t,P_ideal,t)`

` >= 1-w_low - 1/[2(t-1)] - r(2t+1) w_high (1-c_r)^t`.

For fixed `r`, the final polynomial-times-geometric term tends to zero. Hence

`liminf_(t even -> infinity) TV >= 1-gcd(d,3)/d`.

This is not merely the observation that an upper error budget grows. It is a lower bound on the actual readout discrepancy, derived from contraction of actual certified fixed words and a symbolic ideal event. The explicit `c_r=2^(-468602r)` makes the displayed bound entirely quantitative, but its crossover widths can be enormous; no practical or executed width is inferred from it.

### 6.1 Common exact components give an upper bound and sometimes the exact limit

The work eigencomponent `lambda=1` gives readout zero in both algorithms with its full weight `1/r`: every round has `mu=1`, the all-zero history activates no phase, and the one branch is zero. Thus both distributions share the positive subdistribution `(1/r) delta_0`, giving `TV<=1-1/r`.

If `r` is even, the component `lambda=-1` gives another common subdistribution `(1/r) delta_(Q/2)`. In its first `t-1` rounds, the even power in `mu` makes `mu=1`, so every bit is forced zero and `T=I`. In the last round `mu=-1`, still with `T=I`, the zero branch vanishes and the one branch is the identity. Hence its readout is exactly `Q/2`, as in the ideal algorithm. No approximate phase acts on this component.

It follows that for even `r`,

`TV(P_K33,t,P_ideal,t)<=1-2/r`.

For `r=2p` with `p>=5` prime, the lower bound of Section 6 is `1-1/p=1-2/r`. The two estimates therefore give the exact limiting value

`lim_(t even -> infinity) TV = 1-1/p`.

One must not replace this with `TV -> 1` at a fixed `p`. The supremum over all permitted input families is one because `p` can then be chosen arbitrarily large.

## 7. A fixed-order family at the standard width

Fix any odd prime `p>=5`. For every integer `m>=0`, define

`a=18m+4`,

`q=Phi_(2p)(a)=(a^p+1)/(a+1)`,

`N=(a-1)q`.

These are only a mathematical family used to disprove a universal accuracy claim. The factors and order are not supplied to an algorithmic run.

The polynomial has the alternating expansion

`q=a^(p-1)-a^(p-2)+...-a+1`.

Because `a` is even, both `a-1` and `q` are odd. Both exceed one. The following facts are exact:

1. Substitution `a=1` gives `q congruent 1 mod (a-1)`, so `gcd(a-1,q)=1`.
2. The constant term gives `q congruent 1 mod a`, so `gcd(a,N)=1`.
3. The integer identity `a^p+1=(a+1)q` directly gives `a^p congruent -1 mod q`; no invertibility of `a+1` modulo `q` is needed. Since `q>2`, the order modulo `q` divides `2p` but does not divide `p`.
4. The only remaining proper divisor possibility is order two. It is impossible because `q>a^2-1`: pairing the alternating terms gives `q>a^(p-2)(a-1)>=a^3(a-1)>a^2-1` for the present `a>=4,p>=5`.

Thus `ord_q(a)=2p`. Modulo `a-1`, the order is one. The two moduli are coprime, so

`ord_N(a)=2p`.

At the half-order exponent `p`, the residue is `+1 mod(a-1)` and `-1 mod q`. Since both coprime factors exceed two, this is neither `+1` nor `-1 mod N`, so the base is good. In fact the two half-order gcds are exactly `a-1` and `q`.

The coprime factors greater than one show that `N` is an odd composite and not a prime power; **no claim that `q` is prime is needed**. Also `2<=a<N-1`, so it is a valid order-finding base. As `m` grows, `N` and its bit length grow without bound, while the order remains `2p`.

With the standard even width `t_m=2 ceil(log2 N_m)`, one has `t_m -> infinity`. The actual orbit action for every family member is the same `2p`-cycle up to a work-label isometry; unused padded work labels never acquire amplitude. The constant `c_(2p)` is therefore uniform along this family. Section 6 yields

`lim_(m -> infinity) TV(P_K33,N_m,a_m,t_m, P_ideal,N_m,a_m,t_m) = 1-1/p`.

For any proposed uniform tolerance `epsilon<1`, choose a prime `p` with `1-1/p>epsilon`. The displayed limit then forces the TV to exceed that tolerance for sufficiently large members of this standard-width family.

## 8. Every member also avoids the perfect-power precheck

Being non-prime-power does not by itself exclude a composite perfect power such as a product of two prime powers with a common exponent. The chosen family removes that peripheral ambiguity directly, without any additional restriction on `p` or `m`.

Indeed

`a-1=18m+3=3(6m+1)`.

Thus `v_3(a-1)=1`. As `gcd(a-1,q)=1`, also `v_3(N)=1`. Every such `N` is therefore not a perfect power of any exponent at least two. The whole infinite family has order `2p`, the good-base property, and the exact TV limit above.

For a purely algebraic small illustration, `p=5,m=0` gives `a=4,q=205,N=615`. Here `gcd(a+1,q)=5`, showing concretely why that unneeded coprimality must not be imposed. The order and good-base proof still apply. This illustration is not a new executed order-finding run.

The family ensures that the usual even-number and perfect-power preprocessing does not remove these inputs before order finding. It still does not convert a fixed-base raw-readout TV theorem into a theorem about a random-base mixture or final factor output; those require their own analysis.

## 9. Audit result and scope retained

The finite-family contraction, exceptional spectral weight, ideal peak-tail estimate, realification accounting, and standard-width input family all support the claimed obstruction. The statements needing care are now explicit:

- the explicit constant `c_r=2^(-468602r)` is valid uniformly for fixed order and requires no mask enumeration;
- contraction of one branch uses completeness and the lower bound on the other branch;
- the ideal law is the uniform work-spectrum mixture, including the two conjugate internal eigenlines correctly;
- the lower bound concerns the given-base raw readout, not every downstream output law;
- the shared `lambda=+1,-1` components give the matching upper bound for the final family, so its fixed-`p` limit is `1-1/p`, not one;
- the family `a=18m+4` has `v_3(N)=1`, excluding all perfect powers;
- no finite large input was executed, and the enormous symbolic bound is not presented as a practical accuracy threshold.

This obstruction leaves the original CF-only positive-success and finite-retry theorem intact. It establishes a separate limitation: the same fixed K33 compiled readout law cannot uniformly approximate ideal Shor to any one tolerance below one over all inputs, even though it has a provable nonzero factor-success event on every good base.
